new_statements.quote: All Bs speech varieties except some dialects of Kuy and Tsg retain phonemic accent. The following minimal pair is found in all dialects and establishes contrastive accent for PBS: púnuq [pú:nuq] tree trunk < PBS *púnuq and punúq [punúq] full < PBS *punúq. [p.216] ... (1) CANONICAL FORM. In all Bs dialects studied, a closed penult is stressed. Thus, stress is predictable from the shape of the form: all dialects síŋsiŋ ring < PBS *síŋsiŋ, all dialects búkbuk weevil < PBS *búkbuk. [p.218]

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Checked on the page images pages/Zorc 1977 p.216) and pages/p.218) under (also present in the extracted text layer, with scanned noise). Both quoted passages are on the page verbatim: p.216 §8.10 PROTO BISAYAN ACCENT "All Bs speech varieties except some dialects of Kuy and Tsg retain phonemic accent. The following minimal pair is found in all dialects and establishes contrastive accent for PBS: púnuq [pú:nuq] tree trunk < PBS *púnuq and punúq [punúq] full < PBS *punúq." and p.218 §8.10.2 "(1) CANONICAL FORM. In all Bs dialects studied, a closed penult is stressed. Thus, stress is predictable from the shape of the form: all dialects síŋsiŋ ring < PBS *síŋsiŋ, all dialects búkbuk weevil < PBS…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Ratagnon, like every Bisayan dialect other than Cuyonon and Jolo Tausug, has contrastive (phonemic) word accent: the stem is accented either on the penult or on the ultima and this must be learned per lexeme (púnuq 'tree trunk' vs punúq 'full'). An accented open penult has a long vowel; the ultima is never long. Only when the penult is closed (CVC) is accent predictable — it then falls on the penult.
new_statements.exceptions: Cuyonon (Kuy) and Jolo Tausug (Tsg) have lost contrastive accent and regularised stress to the last syllable (§8.10.1, n.82) — this does NOT include Datagnon/Ratagnon, which Zorc groups with the accent-retaining dialects. Closed penult always stressed (except Kuy); PBS *e in an open penult pushed stress to the ultima (p.218); verb vs. stative accent pairs (tápus 'finish' : tapús 'finished'); compensatory lengthening from lost consonants.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level lexical accent (vowel length + stress) on the stem in citation forms; Zorc adds (p.50) that stress is also 'a syntactic feature, a means of counting the full words in a clause' and that the typical stress pattern 'can be overridden by certain intonation patterns' (pp.50-51). The statement is a blanket one over the 36 Bisayan dialects surveyed; Ratagnon ('Datagnon', no. 11, data 'full') is explicitly among them, and Zorc's Datagnon field notes (saved) mark accent on penult or ultima on every elicited form.
new_statements.identity_note: Zorc's 'Datagnon' (Dtg; local name dinatágnun; Ilin Island and Magsaysay, Occidental Mindoro; other names Ratagnun, Latagnun) = Ratagnon [btn], rata1245; his 1972 field-note informant was from San Jose, Occ. Mindoro, living in Bulalacao, Or. Mindoro. 'Santa Teresa' (Zorc's dialect no. 30, data incomplete) is a distinct Kuyan variety of Magsaysay that Glottolog folds into btn. The stress statement is Zorc's family-wide generalisation over all surveyed Bisayan dialects (Ratagnon explicitly included with full data), not a Ratagnon-only description; the Kuyonon (cuyo1237) loss of accent does not apply to Ratagnon.

sources.note: Ratagnon is dialect no. 11 'Datagnon (WBs), dinatágnun, Ilin I. and Magsaysay, Occidental Mindoro; other names Ratagnun, Latagnun; data: full' (Table 2, p.14). §3.1.3 p.50: in all Bs dialects except Kuyonon/Tausug accent = vowel length + stress; accented open penult is long, unaccented/closed syllables and the ultima short; closed penult always accented (except Kuy). §8.10 p.216: all Bs varieties except some Kuy/Tsg dialects retain phonemic accent; minimal pair púnuq 'tree trunk' vs punúq 'full' in all dialects. §8.10.2 p.218: closed penult stressed in all dialects studied; *e in open penult…
Bibliographic only: sole descriptive reference Zorc 1977; alternative names Aradigi, Bisaya, Datagnon, Lactan, Latagnun, Latan.
Numerals and comparison tables drawn from Barbian 1977; no stress information.

sources.note: No prose statement. Every elicited form is marked for lexical accent, on penult or ultima: kanákon, kanímo, kanána, kanámun, kanátun, kanínyu, kanánda; akó, kitá, sánda, dígi, dató, báta?, bukún, mayáman, táwo, baláy, arumán, ka?ápun, paléŋki, nagbakál, tápus, bílug, ŋáran — corroborates contrastive penult/ultima accent in Ratagnon.

sources.note: Santa Teresa = Zorc's dialect no. 30 (data 'incomplete'), folded into Ratagnon [btn] by Glottolog. Accent-marked forms only (ára?, índi?, bakál, súra?, arumán, agód); no prose on stress.
